description: Incident Desk — emergency briefings on live security incidents through an identity lens (machine identity, CA misissuance, identity supply chains, secret management).
license: Copyright the author; briefs linked back to the source site

briefs.title: This week in identity incidents: eMudhra's CA key was literally the number 4
briefs.description: A certificate authority's guessable private keys, a hijacked LiteLLM pipeline and a wave of AI-key theft show machine identity remains the weak link.

briefs.title: Railway Breach: Why Secrets Stored as Plain Environment Variables Keep Failing
briefs.description: Railway says an intruder accessed and in some cases decrypted customer environment variables, exposing API keys and credentials. Here is what is confirmed, what is still a claim, and what to check now.

briefs.title: Node.js Patches a Brotli RCE — and Three TLS Trust Bypasses for Machine Identity
briefs.description: On 21 October 2026 Node.js shipped ten security fixes across three lines, headlined by a Brotli-decoder flaw that can reach remote code execution through fetch. The quieter story is three TLS hostname-verification bypasses — a machine-identity failure that lets a client trust a certificate it never should.

briefs.title: eMudhra's Weak CA Keys: Why Machine Identity Trust Needs Its Own Audit
briefs.description: eMudhra issued certificates signed with guessable private keys, one literally the number 4, forcing browsers to revoke trust and exposing gaps in how machine identities are verified.

briefs.title: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack: Why Machine Credentials Are the Real Lesson
briefs.description: A trojanised LiteLLM release stole cloud, AI and developer credentials via compromised GitHub accounts. Here's what identity leaders should check now.

briefs.title: OVHcloud CLI Supply-Chain Hijack: Why One Contributor's GitHub Account Mattered
briefs.description: A hijacked contributor account let an attacker swap five OVHcloud CLI releases for secret-stealing builds. Here's what's confirmed, what's claimed, and what to check.

briefs.title: OpenCode's Breach Shows Why Third-Party API Keys Need Treating as Credentials
briefs.description: A breach at OpenCode's Console exposed stored OpenAI, Anthropic and Google keys, leaving some users with unauthorised bills of up to $1,700. Rotation and spend limits are the immediate fix.

briefs.title: This week in identity incidents: a backup vendor's app credential became a skeleton key
briefs.description: A stolen ConnectWise application secret let attackers sign into hundreds of Microsoft 365 tenants with no human login and no MFA to stop them.

briefs.title: BeyondTrust Zero-Day: When the Tool That Grants Access Becomes the Breach
briefs.description: A critical authentication bypass in BeyondTrust Remote Support let suspected Chinese state hackers skip login entirely, harvest stored credentials and move laterally. Patch now and assume compromise.

briefs.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup Breach: What 173 Hijacked M365 Tenants Teach About App Identity
briefs.description: A compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential let attackers sign in to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants, bypassing MFA entirely because the access came from an app identity, not a user.

briefs.title: This week in identity incidents: ASOS's rogue push alert and the supplier identities behind it
briefs.description: A deceived employee, a worm in an npm package and 8.8 million Danish records exposed show third-party access and machine identities remain the weak points.

briefs.title: Tensorlake npm Compromise: Shai-Hulud Worm Shows Machine Identities Need Zero Trust
briefs.description: A malicious Tensorlake SDK release carried the Shai-Hulud credential-stealing worm into AI agent infrastructure, caught within 11 minutes but still exposing tokens, keys and secrets on any machine that installed it.

briefs.title: Google domains hijacked via ccTLD registry breach: the identity lesson in DNS trust
briefs.description: Attackers compromised Ghana, Sierra Leone and American Samoa registries to forge valid certificates for Google and other brands. Here is what is confirmed, what is not, and what to check.

briefs.title: This week in identity incidents: a supplier's access exposed 8.8m Danish ID records
briefs.description: A supplier's access to Denmark's ID register was abused, Trump Mobile customer data was published, and ASOS, Bromcom and Nikkei show the same identity gaps.

briefs.title: Trump Mobile breach: 3,615 customers' data published, and what the attackers claim about how they got in
briefs.description: A ransomware group published data on 3,615 Trump Mobile customers and claims it got in through a partner employee's compromised device. What is confirmed, and what is only claimed.

briefs.title: Denmark's CPR Breach: When a Lookup Number Becomes a Skeleton Key to 8.8 Million Identities
briefs.description: Abuse of a small Danish firm's legitimate register access exposed names, addresses and CPR numbers for 8.8 million people, living and dead. The cause and scale of misuse remain unconfirmed.

briefs.title: ASOS and the push notification that spoke for the attacker: secure the identities that talk to your customers
briefs.description: ASOS app users received an "ASOS HACKED" push alert. What is confirmed, what is only claimed, and seven checks every retailer should make on the identities that can message its customers.
